title: Section 4: General prohibition
requirement: Cities and towns are prohibited from enacting, maintaining, or enforcing rent control of any kind, unless they accept Chapter 40P and adopt voluntary regulations meeting specific statutory conditions.
quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:

title: Section 4(a): Voluntary compliance
requirement: Compliance with municipal rent control regulations is entirely voluntary and uncoerced after six months from the date of initial adoption, and property owners may decline to have their property subjected to the regulation.
exemptions: Property owners or entities declining to have their property subjected to rent control regulation
quoted_span: after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced

title: Section 4(b): Scope and unit exemptions
requirement: Municipal rent control regulations cannot include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion, or removal of properties, and cannot apply to units owned by someone owning less than ten rental units or units with a fair market rent exceeding $400.
key_value: less than ten rental units or fair market rent exceeding $400
exemptions: Rental units owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units, or rental units that have a fair market rent exceeding $400
quoted_span: such regulation may not include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from such regulation, nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400;

title: Section 4(c): Compensation for rent-controlled units
requirement: A municipality adopting rent control must compensate owners of rent-controlled units for the difference between the unit's fair market rent and its below-market rent-controlled rent using the municipality's general funds.
quoted_span: a municipality adopting such regulation shall compensate owners of rent controlled units for each unit in the amount of the difference between the unit's fair market rent and the unit's below market, rent controlled rent, with such compensation coming from the municipality's general funds
